videos.title: Will China’s carmakers crack the European premium market? | FT #shorts
videos.transcript: Will China's car makers crack the European premium market? Just two years after launching its first car, industry insiders say China's largest smartphone maker, Xiaomi, already wants to become one of Europe's top five premium brands. Xiaomi is part of a new wave of tech-focused Chinese electric vehicle makers that are seeking to expand overseas with advanced software and autonomous driving capabilities. Brands such as Xpeng, Li Auto, and Huawei-backed Auto are smaller and less known overseas, but they are increasingly popular in the fiercely competitive Chinese market, especially among young consumers. Already more established Chinese brands, including BYD and Chery, have together grabbed a 9% share of the EU car market and 15% in the UK. Compared with mainstream domestic car makers known for their affordable and reliable models, analysts say the new EV makers are stars in terms of the cool factor. Both the newer and bigger Chinese brands are looking to crack the European premium market in the pursuit of bigger profit margins as growth in the home market slows. Some dealers are skeptical about the success of smaller Chinese brands in higher-end markets due to the historic strength of German premium brands. The tech-focused companies, such as Xiaomi and Li Auto, also do not sell vehicles through traditional dealerships, an approach that has proved challenging in the past. But Xiaomi is still convinced that its technological edge and autonomous driving will win over new fans.
videos.summary: The video explores whether Chinese electric vehicle makers can break into the European premium car market. It looks at brands like Xiaomi, BYD, and Xpeng, which are growing in popularity in China and now targeting higher-end European consumers. videos.transcript: Canadian authorities say over 800 fires are currently burning across the country, many of which are classified as being out of control. I understand Ontario currently has over 130 active fires and the smoke is now choking cities as far away as Chicago and New York. How unusual is a smoke event of this scale and reach? >> It's a bit unusual, especially for Ontario. So each of the last few years has been pretty bad for us when it comes to wildfire intensity starting with 2023 in particular and then from there we've had bad wildfire seasons. None of them have really hit Ontario as badly as it is happening this year. So this year it's Ontario and Quebec that are leading in that front. Um, so it it's pretty bad and the wildfire smoke that we're experiencing is a little bit unprecedented in the sense that it hasn't come from Ontario before, but we have been experiencing very bad wildfire smoke seasons since 2023 each summer up until this one. >> What does smoke exposure at this level do to people, especially over the course of several days? >> It can be very harmful. So wildfire smoke is not made up of our usual smoke because it's burning through everything, you know, including properties and cars and fuel. So we're breathing that in and the particles are so small that they can make it all the way into our bloodstream. Um it can have major impacts for really for everybody as you saw in those interviews. Uh make sure to stay indoors in a cool space that has a good filter so that the air is constantly being filtered. And if you don't have that in your home, go to a cool center. We have many open in the area in in all of the cities around where this is happening. Uh so just find out where those are and take a break from from the smoke. >> It sounds like good advice. Uh do you see this becoming the new normal that places hundreds of miles from the fires having to plan for an emergency like this every summer? >> Unfortunately, uh to me we're headed that way. So we've had these kind of summers now since 2023. Parts of our nation have been having these summers since before that. Uh but we've seen a real rise in our wildfire activity over these last few years and our wildfire smoke has impacted all the way to Europe like the one in 2023. My expectation is that we'll continue to see this if we don't make any other changes when it comes obviously to climate change and reducing our emissions um and how we manage our forests as well. Uh so Canada's doing a lot on that front, but we've got a ways to go. Um, but if we don't do anything to slow down climate change, we're going to continue to have these kind of summers with the this type of wildfire smoke. >> Now, I was just looking at some of the information coming through and it it suggests that this year's fires in Canada have burned much less ground than the huge fires there three years ago. You mentioned 2023. Why is the smoke impact so severe if the fire footprint is comparatively smaller? It's a little bit smaller, but we're actually on track to be very similar to our second third worst uh wildfire seasons, and it's in a different part of the country. So, the wildfires that we're having are occurring, especially in our boreal region. They're being started by lightning and spreading very quickly. So, those fires can get very, very large um and consume much more land than fires that happen closer to communities. They're hard harder to control and so they become very big. Um and it's also the type of wildfire. So once they start burning those plumes go up um and they can create their own storms and that it just kind of keeps going and going and it the the smoke is blown south uh due to different type of like the jetream or or different wind patterns. Um so even though it's not as much land as 2023, it's still quite a bit that's burned at this point. >> Well, I hope Ontario and the rest of Canada sees a little rain where these fires are burning. Now, Annabella Bonada from the University of Wateroo in Canada. Thank you so much. >> Thank you for having me.

videos.transcript: Yep, as an American living in Germany, I'm honestly still shocked about what can be played on radio and TV here. Meanwhile, in the US, the FCC can penalize stations for airing indecent content between these times. But the Germans take a different approach. This would far surpass their previous record-breaking tour, which earned around $246 million.
